headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,456 AS FED HIKE FEARS RETURN; Metal Still 32% Above Year-Ago Levels
snippet: Gold fell 0.74% to $4,456.80/oz on June 3 as markets begin pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike before year-end; inflation fears are being driven by deadlocked US-Iran peace negotiations sustaining elevated oil prices, even as the metal remains 32% above its year-ago level.

headline: U.S. DOE AWARDS $134M TO PULL RARE EARTHS FROM WASTE STREAMS IN LOUISIANA AND OKLAHOMA
snippet: Two projects will process bauxite tailings (Colorado School of Mines/ElementUSA, Louisiana) and industrial waste (Phoenix Tailings/MIT, Oklahoma), targeting 150–1,000 metric tons of rare earth output annually from previously discarded material — part of Washington's push to cut Chinese supply chain dependence.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER HITS 5,100 G/T Ag OVER 2M AND 2,176 G/T OVER 8.4M AT MOROCCO'S ZGOUNDER MINE
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported bonanza-grade intercepts at multiple zones of its Zgounder silver mine in Morocco, including 739 g/t Ag over 10m and 1,867 g/t over 6m from the open-pit area; CEO says results confirm strong continuity of mineralization with 30.8% of the 2026 drill program complete.

headline: SILVER CLIMBS TO $76.67 AS SIXTH STRAIGHT YEAR OF SUPPLY DEFICIT WIDENS TO 46.3 MOZ
snippet: Silver rose 1.87% on June 2 as the Silver Institute projects a 46.3 million-ounce supply shortfall in 2026 — the widest deficit in the current six-year run — with a surge in investment demand via coins, bars, and ETPs overwhelming industrial cutbacks driven by sustained high prices.

headline: PACIFIC BOOKER BOARD CALLS AMERICAN EAGLE GOLD'S C$31M BID 'FINANCIALLY INADEQUATE,' SEEKS RIVAL SUITORS
snippet: Independent advisor INFOR Financial says American Eagle Gold's C$1.76/share unsolicited offer for Pacific Booker Minerals (TSXV: BKM) fails to reflect fair value of the Morrison copper-gold project in BC; the board has opened a dataroom and is in talks with multiple alternative strategic parties.

headline: COPPER HOLDS ABOVE $6.50/LB AFTER TRUMP TARIFF MOVE; CHILE POSTS WEAKEST APRIL OUTPUT IN 23 YEARS
snippet: Copper futures held above $6.50/lb after President Trump signed a proclamation adjusting national-security metals tariffs, widening the US copper premium and pulling fresh supply toward US ports; Chile's April production — the world's largest source — hit a 23-year low, tightening the global picture further.

headline: BUNKER HILL MINE CATE-8 SILVER-LEAD ZONE HITS 11.34 OZ/TON AgEq OVER 15.5 FT; JUNE RESTART ON TRACK
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR) expanded the Cate-8 vein to a conceptual target of 50,174–167,821 tons grading 5.75–9.32 oz/ton AgEq at its historic Idaho mine; the 1,800-tpd operation is on track for a June 2026 restart, and management believes the new zone could restore the mine's 50% silver blend ahead of schedule.

headline: GHANA STARTS BUYING 30% OF BIG MINERS' GOLD OUTPUT — NATION TARGETS 157 TONNES IN RESERVES BY 2028
snippet: Ghana's central bank began purchasing 30% of large-scale domestic gold output effective June 1 — up from 20% — under the GANRAP reserve-accumulation framework; the Bank of Ghana is switching to doré gold to build local refining capacity, with a 0.6% price discount agreed with producers.

headline: PERU'S JUNE 7 RUNOFF PUTS BILLIONS IN COPPER AND GOLD INVESTMENT ON THE LINE
snippet: Fujimori vs. Sánchez on June 7 offers sharply divergent futures for Peru's mining sector: a left-wing Sánchez government would raise royalties, review existing contracts, and expand state control, while informal miners have already encroached on MMG's Las Bambas copper mine; business confidence hit a two-year low in April.

headline: URANIUM STEADIES AT $85/LB AS META AND MICROSOFT SIGN NUCLEAR DEALS FOR AI DATA CENTERS
snippet: Uranium spot held near $85/lb after pulling back from a January year-high of $101.41/lb; long-term sentiment remains bullish as AI hyperscalers Meta and Microsoft sign agreements for new nuclear capacity, reinforcing demand growth that pushed uranium 19.5% above year-ago prices despite the recent spot retreat.

headline: MINERS BEAT BULLION — AGAIN: GDX UP 79% VS GOLD'S 36% AS $2,800/OZ MARGINS HOLD EVEN IN PULLBACK
snippet: Gold producers are generating approximately $2,800/oz operating margins with all-in sustaining costs still below $2,000/oz — margins that are holding even as gold retreats from peak; GDX has gained 79% over the past twelve months versus gold's 36%, while the junior miner index GDXJ delivered 203%.
